verdict_gloss: No published work applies a Cohn-Elkies/Delsarte certificate to a target of the form max(0, band-limited) minus a band-limited square, and no published theorem decides whether the LP value equals the one-dimensional lattice value for such a target. The route is not known-dead: neither a priori killer applies. It is not known-live either: the published dimension-1 sharpness theorem is restricted to completely monotone potentials.

part1a_route_applied_to_this_f.answer: not to this f; the same test-function class has been used in the same dimension against the same object
part1a_route_applied_to_this_f.why: Carneiro-Milinovich-Ramos bound a one-dimensional pair functional over the zeros of zeta using the Cohn-Elkies test-function class explicitly 'going beyond the usual class of bandlimited functions', with sign conditions on the transform (ghat(alpha) <= 0 for |alpha| >= 1), solved by SDP.

part1a_lp_tight_in_dim1.packing: sharp in dimension 1, trivially (Cohn PCMI Lecture 5, Exercise 4.1; Li arXiv:2206.09876 calls d=1 trivial)
part1a_lp_tight_in_dim1.energy: sharp in dimension 1 for completely monotone potentials, by explicit magic functions (Cohn-Kumar, JAMS 20 (2007)), construction relying on a variant of the Whittaker-Shannon sampling formula
part1a_lp_tight_in_dim1.reason: the parent's f oscillates and changes sign; it is not a completely monotone function of squared distance

part1b_nonbandlimited_positive_part.reason: the Cohn-Kumar energy LP majorises completely monotone potentials, which are not band-limited; the auxiliary function is not band-limited either
part1b_nonbandlimited_positive_part.mature_technology_for_awkward_targets: Beurling-Selberg (sgn, indicators, x_+ via Graham-Vaaler, wide even classes via Gaussian subordination, arXiv:1008.4969)
part1b_nonbandlimited_positive_part.why_it_does_not_transfer: Beurling-Selberg constrains the SUPPORT of the transform and optimises L1 error; the parent constrains the SIGN of the transform with no support restriction. Different cones, different extremisers.
part1b_nonbandlimited_positive_part.found_nothing_on: one-sided approximation to max(0, D) with D band-limited, under either constraint class

part2_sharpness_theorem.criterion_packing: f proves a sharp bound for a lattice Lambda iff f(x) = 0 for all x in Lambda\{0} and fhat(t) = 0 for all t in Lambda*\{0} (Cohn, PCMI notes, Lecture 5)
part2_sharpness_theorem.criterion_energy: f(x) = p(|x|) for x in Lambda\{0} and fhat(y) = 0 for y in Lambda*\{0}, to second order (CKMRV eqs 1.2-1.3)
part2_sharpness_theorem.strong_duality: proved for the Cohn-Elkies LP by Cohn, de Laat, Salmon (arXiv:2206.15373); for Turan and Delsarte on Euclidean space by Kolountzakis, Lev, Matolcsi (arXiv:2510.10172), with tiling-type relations between primal extremal functions and dual extremal measures
part2_sharpness_theorem.why_none_can_exist: in dimension 1 the equidistant lattice is not always the ground state for non-convex potentials: Ventevogel-Nijboer's phi(x) = (1+x^4)^{-1} has a non-equidistant minimiser at high density, so 'LP value equals lattice value in dimension 1' is false as a general statement

actionable_transfer.why: maps feasible points of the infinite-dimensional Cohn-Elkies LP into a finite-dimensional problem, then solves the dual; a dual-feasible point is a LOWER bound on the LP value and proves non-sharpness when it exceeds the target
actionable_transfer.relevance: the parent's kill condition 1 needs a lower bound on V that carries content; a truncated primal solve only ever gives a relaxation, which is why 37fb06a9's 0.0541015 sat below the achievability floor 0.05716501969327026

not_found: any paper applying a Cohn-Elkies/Delsarte certificate to a target of the form max(0, D) - K with D band-limited
any paper on one-sided approximation to the positive part of a band-limited function
any published obstruction specific to positive-part targets
any theorem asserting LP value = lattice value in dimension 1 outside the completely monotone class
any dual-bound computation for a one-dimensional ENERGY linear program (all published discrete-reduction duals are for packing in d >= 3)
not_found_caveat: one web-search backend, no MathSciNet and no zbMATH. These are 'not found by the searches recorded here', not 'do not exist'.

derived_here_not_prior_art.claim: A differentiable majorant G cannot touch f at an upward kink of max(0,D): G >= f with equality at s0 forces G'(s0) <= f'(s0-) and G'(s0) >= f'(s0+), which are incompatible when the derivative jumps up. In the parametrisation G(s) = -int mu(w) cos(sw) dw, G is differentiable when int w mu(w) dw < infinity and real-analytic when mu has compact support, so a bounded frequency grid can never achieve contact at a kink.
derived_here_not_prior_art.consequence: This does not bite for the lattice: run 37fb06a9 section 2 measured P = 0 on the critical lattice out to d = 4000, i.e. every multiple of 2*pi lies inside a depth-1 damage window, so f is smooth exactly where complementary slackness demands contact.

derived_here_not_prior_art.claim: Transporting the published sharpness criterion to Lambda = 2*pi*Z: the dual lattice is (1/(2*pi))Z and Ghat is carried by w = 2*pi*|xi|, so the condition Ghat = 0 on Lambda*\{0} becomes mu(w) = 0 for every nonzero integer w. If V equals the lattice value L/2 = 0.05716501969327026, an optimal mu charges no positive integer and the optimal G touches f on all of 2*pi*Z\{0}.
derived_here_not_prior_art.usable_direction: contrapositive: if a well-conditioned solve returns an optimal mu that charges the integers, or an optimal G whose contact set is not 2*pi*Z\{0}, then V is strictly above the lattice value
